t: In a contributory group term scheme where members pay part of the premium, insurers usually insist on a minimum percentage of eligible employees joining the scheme. The main purpose of this requirement is to:
o: Ensure the employer earns commission
Increase the free cover limit for senior managers
Reduce anti-selection by preventing only unhealthy employees from opting in
Comply with the Payment of Gratuity Act
e: Where joining is voluntary, those in poor health are most likely to enrol. A minimum participation requirement (often 75% or more) keeps the risk pool representative of the whole group.

t: Which of the following lists only products that are written as group life insurance business in India?
o: Group term assurance, group gratuity, group superannuation, group credit life
Individual endowment, group gratuity, motor fleet, group credit life
Group term assurance, fire floater, group superannuation, marine open cover
Key-man insurance, personal accident, group gratuity, householder's policy
e: Group term, group gratuity, group superannuation and group credit life are all life-insurance group products. Fleet, fire floater and marine open cover are general insurance group arrangements.

t: IRDAI's group insurance guidelines require that premium rates quoted for a group be:
o: Identical to the insurer's individual term rates
Approved in advance by the Life Insurance Council
Based on actuarial principles and justified by the appointed actuary, not offered arbitrarily to win business
Fixed by IRDAI through a tariff
e: The guidelines require premium rates to have an actuarial basis certified by the appointed actuary, so that groups are not underpriced for competitive reasons and then subsidised by other policyholders.

t: Under IRDAI norms, which statement about a non-employer-employee group master policyholder is correct?
o: It may receive the claim amount and decide how much to pass to the member
It cannot be a beneficiary of the policy; benefits must flow to members or their nominees
It must contribute at least 50% of the premium
It must be a company registered under the Companies Act
e: In non-employer-employee groups the master policyholder is only a facilitator; IRDAI specifically bars it from being a beneficiary so that members' interests are protected.

t: When a fund-based group gratuity policy is surrendered by the trustees, IRDAI's non-linked product norms allow the insurer to:
o: Forfeit the entire fund value
Apply a market value adjustment and a limited surrender charge, with the balance fund payable to the trustees
Retain the fund until all employees retire
Pay only the employer's original contributions without interest
e: Surrender of fund-based group policies attracts only a capped surrender charge (0.05% of the fund subject to a ceiling of ₹5 lakh under the 2013 regulations) plus any market value adjustment, protecting the members' accumulated fund.

t: Under IRDAI's group guidelines, the master policyholder is required to maintain:
o: A register of members with details of cover, which the insurer may inspect
A separate bank account in the insurer's name
A copy of each member's income-tax return
Medical records of every member for ten years
e: The group policyholder must keep an up-to-date member register (names, dates of entry and exit, sum assured, nominees) and permit the insurer to inspect it, as the insurer relies on this data for pricing and claims.

t: In 2024 IRDAI consolidated the separate regulations on linked, non-linked and other products into a single set of regulations titled:
o: IRDAI (Group Insurance) Regulations, 2024
IRDAI (Life Insurance Tariff) Regulations, 2024
IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations, 2024
IRDAI (Retirement Benefit Products) Regulations, 2024
e: The IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations, 2024 replaced the 2019 linked and non-linked product regulations along with several others, as part of the regulator's rationalisation of its rulebook.

t: In a defined contribution group superannuation scheme, the pension that a member ultimately receives depends on:
o: The member's final salary and years of service as per a fixed formula
The accumulated contributions plus investment earnings and the annuity rate available at retirement
The employer's profits in the year of retirement
The ceiling fixed under the Payment of Gratuity Act
e: In a DC scheme the employer's obligation ends with the contribution; the member bears investment and annuity-rate risk. A final-salary formula characterises a defined benefit scheme.

t: A retiring member of a superannuation scheme chooses an annuity 'with return of purchase price'. Under this option:
o: Annuity is paid for life and on death the purchase price is returned to the nominee
Annuity is paid only for a guaranteed period of 15 years
Annuity increases every year by a fixed percentage
Annuity continues to the spouse at 50% after the member's death
e: Return-of-purchase-price annuities pay a lower annuity rate than a plain life annuity because the capital is returned on death; they are popular in India because the family does not lose the corpus.

topic: Tax Aspects of Group & Retirement Benefit Schemes
t: An employer's contribution to an approved gratuity fund is allowed as a business deduction under which section of the Income-tax Act, 1961?
o: Section 36(1)(iv)
Section 80C
Section 40A(7)
Section 36(1)(v)
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 36(1)(v) allows contributions to an approved gratuity fund created under an irrevocable trust. Section 36(1)(iv) relates to recognised PF and approved superannuation funds, and Section 40A(7) disallows mere provisions for gratuity.

t: A group leave encashment scheme funded with a life insurer is designed to:
o: Pay employees cash in lieu of weekly off days
Build a fund to meet the employer's liability for accumulated privilege leave payable on exit, with the employer's contributions credited to a policy account
Replace the statutory ESI benefit for sickness
Provide life cover equal to the accumulated leave balance of each employee
e: Leave encashment is an employer liability valued actuarially; funding it through an insurer's policy account allows systematic accumulation, with an optional small life cover rider.

t: A common basis for fixing the sum assured of each member under an employer-employee group term scheme is:
o: The member's own choice without any limit
The amount of the member's outstanding personal loans
A multiple of annual salary or a flat amount by grade or designation
The member's provident fund balance
e: Benefit formulas tied to salary or grade are objective and prevent selection by individual members; salary-multiple and grade-wise flat covers are the most common designs.

t: A group term policy covers 1,000 lives of ₹10 lakh each. If the expected mortality rate for the group is 2 per 1,000, the pure risk premium (before expenses and margins) required for the year is:
e: Expected claims = 1,000 × 0.002 = 2 deaths × ₹10 lakh = ₹20 lakh. This equals ₹2 per ₹1,000 sum assured on the total cover of ₹100 crore.

topic: Tax Aspects of Group & Retirement Benefit Schemes
t: For an employee NOT covered by the Payment of Gratuity Act, the gratuity exemption under Section 10(10)(iii) is based on:
o: Half a month's average salary (of the last 10 months) for each completed year of service, subject to the ₹20 lakh ceiling
15/26 of last drawn salary for each year of service
One month's salary for each completed year of service
Ten months' average salary
e: For non-covered employees, exemption is the least of actual gratuity, ₹20 lakh and half month's average salary (average of 10 months preceding retirement) for each completed year of service, ignoring fractions.

topic: Tax Aspects of Group & Retirement Benefit Schemes
t: An employee not covered by the Payment of Gratuity Act retires after 25 years 8 months of service. Average salary of the last 10 months is ₹80,000 and gratuity received is ₹12 lakh. The exempt amount is:
o: ₹12 lakh
₹10 lakh
₹20 lakh
e: Only completed years count (25). Half month's salary × 25 = ₹40,000 × 25 = ₹10 lakh, which is less than the actual ₹12 lakh and the ₹20 lakh ceiling; taxable gratuity is ₹2 lakh.

topic: Tax Aspects of Group & Retirement Benefit Schemes
t: Commutation of pension from an approved superannuation fund is exempt under Section 10(13) up to:
o: One-half of the pension in every case
One-fourth of the pension
One-third of the pension in every case
One-third of the pension if the employee also receives gratuity, otherwise one-half
e: Rule 90 of the Income-tax Rules and Section 10(10A)/(13) allow tax-free commutation of one-third of the pension where gratuity is received and one-half where it is not.

topic: Tax Aspects of Group & Retirement Benefit Schemes
t: Under Section 17(2)(vii) of the Income-tax Act, as amended by the Finance Act, 2020, the aggregate employer contribution to recognised provident fund, NPS and approved superannuation fund is taxed as a perquisite to the extent it exceeds:
o: ₹1.5 lakh per year
₹7.5 lakh per year
₹2.5 lakh per year
₹5 lakh per year
e: The earlier limit of ₹1.5 lakh applied only to superannuation contributions; from FY 2020-21 a combined ceiling of ₹7.5 lakh applies across PF, NPS and superannuation, and the accretion on the excess is also taxable.

topic: Tax Aspects of Group & Retirement Benefit Schemes
t: Under Rules 103 and 104 of the Income-tax Rules, the employer's initial contribution for past service and the ordinary annual contribution to an approved gratuity fund are each limited to:
o: 10% of salary
15% of salary
8⅓% of salary (for each year of past service, in the case of the initial contribution)
27% of salary
e: Rule 104 caps the ordinary annual contribution at 8⅓% of each employee's salary; Rule 103 caps the initial contribution at 8⅓% of salary for each year of past service. Amounts beyond these need specific approval.

t: The annual premium for Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY), which provides ₹2 lakh accidental death and total disability cover, is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). PMSBY premium was raised from ₹12 to ₹20 per annum from June 2022. It covers persons aged 18 to 70 for ₹2 lakh on accidental death or total disability and ₹1 lakh for partial disability.

topic: Tax Aspects of Group & Retirement Benefit Schemes
t: The accumulated balance in a recognised provident fund paid to an employee is fully exempt from tax if the employee has:
o: Rendered continuous service of five years or more (including service with a previous employer whose balance was transferred)
Attained the age of 58 years, irrespective of service
Rendered at least 10 years of service
Contributed at least ₹1 lakh in total
e: Rule 8 of Part A of the Fourth Schedule exempts the balance after five years of continuous service, or earlier if service ends due to ill-health, closure of business or other reasons beyond the employee's control.

t: Under AS 15 (Revised 2005), actuarial gains and losses on a defined benefit plan are:
o: Deferred using the corridor approach
Recognised in other comprehensive income
Recognised immediately in the statement of profit and loss
Ignored until the plan is settled
e: AS 15 (Revised) requires immediate recognition in profit or loss; the corridor approach of the old IAS 19 was never adopted in India, and OCI treatment applies only under Ind AS 19.

t: How is the expense for a defined contribution plan (such as the employer's share of EPF) recognised in the employer's accounts?
o: By an actuarial valuation of the projected benefit
As the contribution payable for the period, with no further obligation
As a percentage of profits set aside as reserve
Only when the employee actually retires
e: In a DC plan the employer's obligation is limited to the agreed contribution; the amount due for the period is charged as expense and any unpaid portion shown as a liability. No actuarial valuation is required.

t: A company's gratuity plan has a defined benefit obligation of ₹150 lakh and plan assets of ₹120 lakh at the start of the year. With a discount rate of 7%, the net interest cost to be charged to profit or loss under Ind AS 19 is:
o: ₹10.5 lakh
₹8.4 lakh
₹30 lakh
₹2.1 lakh
e: Ind AS 19 applies the discount rate to the net defined benefit liability: (150 − 120) × 7% = ₹2.1 lakh. Under AS 15 interest cost (₹10.5 lakh) and expected return on plan assets would be shown separately.

topic: Investment Pattern for Retirement Benefit Schemes
t: Under the IRDAI (Investment) Regulations, funds of a life insurer relating to pension, general annuity and group business must have at least what proportion in Central Government securities?
e: For the pension and general annuity and group fund, the pattern requires not less than 20% in Government securities, not less than 40% in Government and other approved securities taken together, and the balance in approved investments.

topic: Investment Pattern for Retirement Benefit Schemes
t: The current investment pattern adopted by the Central Board of Trustees of EPFO permits investment in equity and related instruments up to:
o: 15% of incremental deposits
5% of incremental deposits
25% of incremental deposits
50% of incremental deposits
e: EPFO follows the 2015 Ministry of Finance pattern, which allows 5% to 15% in equities; the Board has generally invested around the upper end of this band through ETFs.

topic: Investment Pattern for Retirement Benefit Schemes
t: Under the 'Active Choice' option in NPS Tier I, the maximum allocation that a subscriber may make to Asset Class E (equity) is:
e: PFRDA allows up to 75% in equity under Active Choice (with tapering after age 50 in some variants); Asset Class A (alternative investments) is capped at 5%. The 'Auto Choice' life-cycle funds have preset glide paths.

t: The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 applies to every shop or establishment in which the number of persons employed on any day in the preceding 12 months is:
o: 5 or more
20 or more
50 or more
10 or more
e: Section 1(3) extends the Act to factories, mines, oilfields, plantations, ports and railways, and to shops or establishments employing 10 or more persons; once covered, the Act continues to apply even if numbers fall below 10.

t: To be eligible for a monthly member's pension on superannuation under the Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995, a member must have rendered eligible service of at least:
o: 10 years and attained the age of 58
5 years and attained the age of 60
20 years irrespective of age
15 years and attained the age of 55
e: EPS pays monthly pension on completing 10 years of pensionable service and reaching 58. Members with less than 10 years receive a withdrawal benefit instead.

t: A company covers 500 employees under a group term policy with a uniform sum assured of ₹10 lakh each. The insurer quotes a rate of ₹1.20 per ₹1,000 sum assured. The annual premium is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Total sum assured = 500 × ₹10 lakh = ₹50 crore. Premium = ₹50,00,00,000 ÷ 1,000 × 1.20 = ₹6,00,000.

t: A member of EPS 1995 with 22 years of pensionable service opts for early pension at age 54. If the full pension at 58 would be ₹6,000, the reduced pension payable is:
e: Early pension is available from age 50 with a reduction of 4% for each year by which age falls short of 58. Four years short → 16% reduction → ₹6,000 × 0.84 = ₹5,040.

t: A PF member dies in service. His average monthly wages for the preceding 12 months were ₹15,000 and the average PF balance was ₹2 lakh. The EDLI benefit payable to the nominee is:
e: EDLI = 35 × average wages (max ₹15,000) = ₹5,25,000, plus 50% of average PF balance (₹1,00,000, within the ₹1,75,000 cap) = ₹6,25,000. The overall maximum benefit is ₹7 lakh and the minimum ₹2.5 lakh.

t: An NPS subscriber exits the scheme at age 45, before superannuation, with a corpus of ₹20 lakh. Under PFRDA exit regulations she must:
o: Withdraw the full corpus in cash
Use at least 80% of the corpus to purchase an annuity and may withdraw up to 20% as lump sum
Use at least 40% for an annuity
Transfer the corpus to EPF
e: On premature exit (before 60 or before completing the required period), at least 80% must be annuitised; full withdrawal is permitted only if the corpus is ₹2.5 lakh or less.

t: Under the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) for Central Government employees effective 1 April 2025, an employee with 25 years or more of qualifying service receives an assured pension of:
o: 50% of the average basic pay drawn over the last 12 months before superannuation
Two-thirds of last drawn basic pay
40% of the final year's total emoluments
₹10,000 per month flat
e: UPS guarantees 50% of average basic pay of the last 12 months for 25 years of service, with proportionate pension for shorter service (minimum 10 years) and a floor of ₹10,000 per month.

t: Under the Projected Unit Credit method, the 'current service cost' represents:
o: The total gratuity payable if all employees resigned today
The present value of the benefit earned by employees for service rendered during the current year, allowing for projected salary
The interest earned on the plan assets during the year
The contribution the employer actually paid to the fund
e: Current service cost is the increase in the present value of the obligation resulting from employee service in the current period, computed with projected final salaries and discounted to today.

t: Under IRDAI's 2024 norms, a surveyor must be appointed within what time of a claim intimation?
o: 24 hours
48 hours
72 hours
7 days
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Appointment within 24 hours; survey report within 15 days; insurer's decision within 7 days of the report.

t: If all other assumptions are unchanged, an increase in the assumed salary escalation rate used in a gratuity valuation will:
o: Have no effect on the obligation since gratuity depends on last drawn salary
Reduce the defined benefit obligation
Increase the defined benefit obligation
Reduce the discount rate automatically
e: Gratuity is linked to final salary, so projecting higher future salaries raises the expected benefit and therefore the present value of the obligation. The discount rate is set independently.

t: A gratuity payment of ₹10 lakh is expected to fall due exactly two years from the valuation date. Ignoring mortality and withdrawal, its present value at a discount rate of 8% per annum is approximately:
e: PV = ₹10,00,000 ÷ (1.08)² = ₹10,00,000 ÷ 1.1664 = ₹8,57,339. Dividing by 1.08 only once gives ₹9,25,926, which is the one-year value.

t: In a defined benefit valuation, 'past service cost' arises when:
o: Employees complete another year of service
The discount rate falls during the year
The employer amends the scheme to improve benefits for service already rendered
Plan assets earn less than expected
e: Past service cost is the change in the obligation for prior-period service caused by a plan amendment or curtailment, e.g. raising the gratuity ceiling. Other items are current service cost, actuarial loss and asset return shortfall respectively.

topic: Group Insurance - Administration, Claims and Renewals
t: A new employee joins an employer-employee group term scheme three months before the policy anniversary. The annual premium for her cover is ₹1,200. The premium normally charged for the balance period is:
e: Mid-term additions are charged pro-rata premium for the unexpired period: ₹1,200 × 3/12 = ₹300. Similarly, pro-rata refunds are given for deletions.

topic: Group Insurance - Administration, Claims and Renewals
t: On the death of a member under an insurer-funded group gratuity scheme, the claim amount is paid by the insurer to:
o: Directly to the nominee of the employee under the EPF nomination
The trustees of the gratuity fund, who settle the gratuity with the employee's nominee or legal heirs
The Regional Provident Fund Commissioner
The employer's current account for distribution
e: The master policy is held by the trustees; the insurer pays them and they discharge the gratuity liability to the beneficiary, keeping the fund separate from the employer's own monies.

topic: Group Insurance - Administration, Claims and Renewals
t: A member leaves the employer during the policy year. Under a group term policy the usual practice is that:
o: Cover ceases on the date of exit and pro-rata premium for the unexpired period is refunded
Cover continues to the policy anniversary and no refund is given
Cover continues for life as a paid-up policy
The employer must continue paying premium for the ex-employee
e: Group cover depends on membership; it ends when the member leaves. Some policies offer a conversion option allowing the member to take individual cover within a specified period without medical examination.

topic: Group Insurance - Administration, Claims and Renewals
t: Which of the following is an important administrative responsibility of the master policyholder at each renewal of a group term policy?
o: Submitting audited financial statements of the company to IRDAI
Obtaining a medical report from every member
Furnishing updated member data (age, salary or grade, sum assured, additions and deletions) to enable the insurer to re-rate the premium
Depositing the premium with the Life Insurance Council
e: Renewal premium is recalculated on current membership and benefit data; accurate data from the master policyholder is essential for correct rating and for avoiding disputes at claim stage.

t: For health insurance, the maximum time an insurer may take to decide a cashless authorisation request under the 2024 master circular is:
o: 1 hour
3 hours
6 hours
24 hours
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Cashless authorisation within 1 hour of request; final discharge authorisation within 3 hours.

t: Under a quota share reinsurance treaty, the ceding insurer:
o: Cedes only risks that exceed its retention
Cedes a fixed percentage of every risk within the treaty scope, and receives the same percentage of premium less commission
Cedes only catastrophe losses above a threshold
Cedes risks on a case-by-case basis after negotiation
e: Quota share is proportional reinsurance with a fixed share on every risk; it is simple to administer and useful for new or small insurers, but it also cedes the premium on small risks the insurer could retain.

t: A life insurer writing a group term scheme has one member with a sum assured of ₹15 crore, far above its treaty's automatic acceptance limit. The appropriate reinsurance arrangement for this life is:
o: No reinsurance, since group policies are exempt
Catastrophe excess of loss cover
Facultative reinsurance for that individual life
Quota share on the whole group only
e: Facultative reinsurance is negotiated individually for risks that fall outside the automatic treaty capacity, such as very large or substandard lives in a group.

t: Any alteration to the rules of an approved superannuation or gratuity fund is effective for tax purposes only if:
o: The employees' union agrees in writing
The alteration is approved by the Commissioner of Income-tax (or the prescribed income-tax authority)
IRDAI issues a no-objection certificate
The life insurer amends the master policy
e: Under the Fourth Schedule, the trustees must communicate any rule change to the Commissioner, and the fund's approval may be withdrawn if the alteration is not accepted.

t: An employee moves from Company A to Company B, both of which have approved superannuation funds. The accumulated balance in A's fund is:
o: Forfeited to Company A as the employee resigned
Paid to the employee as a taxable lump sum only
Transferable to Company B's approved fund without being treated as income of the employee
Compulsorily converted to an annuity immediately
e: Transfer of the balance between approved superannuation funds on change of employment is permitted and is not taxed at that stage; the benefit continues to accumulate until retirement.

t: Atal Pension Yojana (APY) is open to Indian citizens in the age group of:
o: 18 to 50 years
25 to 55 years
18 to 70 years
18 to 40 years
e: APY enrols persons aged 18 to 40 so that contributions run for at least 20 years before the guaranteed pension of ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 per month starts at age 60; since October 2022 income-tax payers cannot join.

t: The wage ceiling for coverage of an employee under the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 (other than persons with disability) is:
o: ₹21,000 per month
₹15,000 per month
₹25,000 per month
₹30,000 per month
e: The ESI wage ceiling was raised to ₹21,000 from 1 January 2017 (₹25,000 for employees with disability). The scheme applies to non-seasonal factories and notified establishments with 10 or more employees.

t: Under the Code on Social Security, 2020, a fixed-term employee becomes eligible for gratuity on a pro-rata basis after completing continuous service of:
o: Three years
Two years
Five years
One year
e: The Code reduces the gratuity qualifying period for fixed-term employees to one year, while the five-year rule continues for others; working journalists qualify after three years.
